contested.name: Ex- Servicemen Contributory Health Scheme
contested.the_argument_against: an ex-serviceman and his dependants are people, they enrol, they hold a card, and they receive treatment. myScheme lists 52 ex-servicemen schemes, so it plainly serves this population.
contested.the_argument_for_the_label: the Union pays it as an employer to its own retired soldiers, which parse/classify_tamilnadu.py established over 829 labels is not a welfare scheme. myScheme has no record for this or for CGHS, and its six central records for ex-servicemen are all discretionary welfare-fund grants, one explicitly for non-pensioner ex-servicemen.
contested.what_would_flip_it: myScheme listing CGHS or any other health scheme whose eligibility is government service. It lists none today.

contested.name: Duty Drawback Scheme
contested.the_argument_against: myScheme does list exporter schemes, the Export Promotion Capital Goods Scheme among them, and the CAG audited that one too. So the portal has a place for a scheme of this shape, and its absence is not nothing.
contested.the_argument_for_the_label: the claimant is a firm and the payment is a refund of customs and excise duty the firm itself paid, not a benefit conferred on a beneficiary.
contested.what_would_flip_it: treating a firm as a citizen for this purpose. The register does not, and neither does myScheme's own beneficiary vocabulary, which separates Individual and Family from Business Entity and Industries.

contested.name: Member of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme (MPLAD)
contested.the_argument_against: the money reaches individuals through what the works build, and a citizen can ask an MP for a work.
contested.the_argument_for_the_label: released to a district authority for works a Member of Parliament recommends. The unit of spending is a work in a constituency and no list of individual beneficiaries exists. myScheme lists no constituency development scheme of any kind, at the union or in any state.
contested.what_would_flip_it: a beneficiary list. Asking an MP is not an application and produces no record a register could read.

contested.name: National Mission for a Green India
contested.the_argument_against: most of the money buys forest cover on public land, which is an asset, and the recipient of record is a state forest department.
contested.the_argument_for_the_label: DBT Bharat lists it and the mission's own design pays forest-dependent households for plantation and protection work.
contested.what_would_flip_it: dropping the DBT listing as evidence. It is the strongest government-supplied signal in this file at 0.820 over 50, and this is the row where it is doing the most work.

contested.name: Samagra Shiksha
contested.the_argument_against: most of the Rs 42,100 crore is teacher salaries and school infrastructure, and no parent applies to Samagra Shiksha.
contested.the_argument_for_the_label: DBT Bharat lists its textbook intervention and the Outcome Budget counts students given free textbooks, children given transport and children given escorts. A child is the beneficiary of record for those.
contested.what_would_flip_it: labelling umbrella programmes by where most of the money goes rather than by whether a person is a beneficiary of record anywhere in them. That rule would also move Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojna and Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojna, and it is stated as the tie-break in data/cag/citizen_labels.json so it can be reversed in one place.

contested.name: Scheme for Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of (Hybrid and) Electric Vehicle in India - (FAME - India).
contested.the_argument_against: it is routed through the manufacturer, who is reimbursed, and the buyer never handles the money.
contested.the_argument_for_the_label: the demand incentive lowers the price an identified buyer pays and the buyer is verified before it is paid. DBT Bharat lists the delivery mechanism by name.
contested.what_would_flip_it: requiring the payment to land in the beneficiary's own hands. That would also move the free textbooks under Samagra Shiksha and every in-kind transfer DBT Bharat lists.

population.how_chosen: a census of the schemes the CAG join published as audited at the time of labelling, 20 of them, plus a stratified sample of the 701 registry entries that myScheme does not list, which is the population the distinction is applied to. The strata and the steps are fixed and published so the sample can be rebuilt: sorted by name within each stratum, take every k-th.
population.note: 134 drawn, 20 audited, 153 distinct after the overlap. The audited set moves whenever parse/match.py or the register moves, so parse/cag_join.py reads it live rather than from the audited_when_labelled flag below, and prints a warning if an audited scheme has no label here.

rule.borderline: marked where a reader could reasonably flip the label, and the reason on the row carries the argument the other way.
rule.budget_line: the recipient of record is a government, a public body, an institution, a firm acting as a firm, an asset or a work. Citizens may benefit from what it buys, and often do, but no individual is a beneficiary of record and no list of individuals exists.
rule.citizen_scheme: the benefit reaches an identified person or household, or a group of individuals such as a self-help group: cash, an in-kind good, a scholarship or stipend, a pension, an insurance cover, a subsidy on something they buy, a treatment, a house, a connection, a wage, a training place, a loan or a fee waiver. Somebody could produce the list of who received it.
rule.not_a_verdict_on_the_spending: a budget_line label says nothing against the spending. Roads, courts, research and rolling stock are what a state is for. The label says only that a citizen scheme portal is not where you would look for them.
rule.the_one_exclusion: an employer obligation is not a citizen scheme. The government pays it as an employer to its own serving or retired staff and their families. This line is not invented here: parse/classify_tamilnadu.py established it over 829 hand labels and this register already publishes it, so applying it at the union is consistency rather than a new judgement.
rule.the_tie_break: an umbrella programme is labelled by its principal deliverable, not by the existence of one individual-facing component. Where the principal deliverable is contested the row is labelled on the government's own evidence, which is a DBT Bharat listing or an Outcome Budget target counted in people, and marked borderline.
rule.what_is_NOT_the_test: whether an application exists. That is the intuitive test and it does not survive measurement: see signals_rejected in data/cag/join.json. It is also not computable for the 701 register rows myScheme does not list, which is the population the distinction is for.

citizen_test.question: Of the things a government funds, which reach an identified person or household, so that a portal built for citizens to look schemes up would have a page for them? This decides whether 'absent from myScheme' is a criticism of the portal or a fact about the spending, and it is why the absent list below is two lists.

rule.clause: an employer obligation is never a citizen scheme
rule.detail: the government pays it as an employer to its own serving or retired staff and their families. Not invented here: parse/classify_tamilnadu.py established this over 829 hand labels and the register already publishes it, so applying it at the union is consistency rather than a fresh judgement.
rule.measured: P(citizen scheme) 0.000 over the 3 labelled rows it fires on, which is a small number and is stated as one. The weight of the evidence is Tamil Nadu's 829 labels and myScheme's own catalogue: the portal lists neither ECHS nor CGHS, and all six of its central records for ex-servicemen are discretionary grants from the Armed Forces Flag Day Fund and the Raksha Mantri's Ex-Servicemen Welfare Fund, one of them explicitly for non-pensioner ex-servicemen.

rule.clause: a grant to a body is not a benefit to a person, even when a payment sits inside it
rule.detail: the name has to say so with a preposition: assistance, grants, support, compensation, payments or reimbursement TO a board, council, institute, federation, agency, state, school, company or industry.
rule.measured: P(citizen scheme) 0.000 over 4. It is what separates Assistance to National Sports Federations and Grants to VV Giri National Labour Institute, both of which DBT Bharat lists because a stipend is paid inside them, from the schemes that pay a person directly.

rule.clause: otherwise the signals score and the total decides
rule.detail: weights are the measurements rounded, not a feeling: the three signals above 0.82 are worth 3, the benefit phrase at 0.865 is worth 2 because it overlaps the beneficiary word, the two name signals near 0.11 are worth -2, and the sector at 0.053 is worth -1 because it fires on more rows than any of them and should not decide a row alone.
rule.measured: threshold 2. On the 153 hand labels precision 0.915, recall 0.900, accuracy 0.928, counted and not estimated.

rule.clause: the threshold is the accuracy-maximising one, not the precision-buying one
rule.detail: every other classifier in this repository trades recall away for precision, because each of them decides an absence claim and one wrong accusation costs more than ten missing ones. This test decides no absence: both sides of the split are published, each under its own heading, so a row on the wrong side is miscategorised rather than accused. The cost is symmetric and the operating point follows.
rule.measured: accuracy 0.908 at threshold 1, 0.928 at 2, 0.915 at 3. Threshold 3 would move FAME to the wrong side of the published split.

signals_rejected.measured_over: the schemes the join listed as audited when these labels were made, hand read one by one as a census of that list. It is the only signal here that no source in the register carries.
signals_rejected.signal: whether a citizen can apply for it
signals_rejected.why_not: no signal and slightly the wrong sign. The schemes that reach the most people select beneficiaries from a list rather than take applications, and PMAY-Gramin, Ayushman Bharat and Jal Jeevan Mission all fall on the no-application side while the Duty Drawback Scheme and the Ex-Servicemen Contributory Health Scheme both have a form. It is also not computable for the 701 rows myScheme does not list, which is the population the test is for.

signals_rejected.signal: the union budget's own Statement 4A against Statement 4B
signals_rejected.why_not: no signal. Centrally Sponsored against Central Sector says who delivers the money, states or the union directly, and nothing about who receives it. Statement 4B holds Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana and Rolling Stock alike.

signals_rejected.signal: an Outcome Budget target counted in people
signals_rejected.why_not: no signal, and it fires on 10 of 153 rows because only 111 register entries carry an outcome framework at all. The indicator text in data/outcome/2026.json is also the first line of a wrapped cell, so 'Number of children provided Transport' and 'Number of schools covered under' are both truncated mid-phrase and the unit is often the part that was cut.

signals_rejected.signal: the size of the budget line, Rs 1,000 crore or more
signals_rejected.why_not: no signal at any threshold, which is worth publishing because it is the assumption a reader brings. Rolling Stock is Rs 52,109 crore and reaches nobody as a beneficiary; the Sugar Subsidy under the Public Distribution System is Rs 200 crore and reaches Antyodaya households.

signals_rejected.signal: data/classification.json's own scheme-versus-budget-head score, 4 or more
signals_rejected.why_not: weak, and circular for this question. parse/classify.py states in its own docstring that it is validated against myScheme membership as the proxy for citizen-facing. Scoring a row on a classifier trained to agree with myScheme, in order to decide whether myScheme should have listed it, answers the question with itself. The same reasoning is set out in parse/classify_andhra.py's why_not_myscheme and in signals_rejected above.

signals_rejected.signal: whether myScheme lists the row at all
signals_rejected.why_not: the strongest circular signal there is. The finding this file exists to publish is which audited schemes are ABSENT from myScheme, so scoring myScheme presence would push down exactly the rows the answer is made of. What IS used is different and is stated as such: myScheme's own targetBeneficiaries tag on the rows it does list, which disagrees with myScheme's inclusion decision twice among the audited schemes it does list, at AMRUT and at the Export Promotion Capital Goods Scheme.

rule.borderline_note: The hardest calls are umbrella against component and national scheme against a state's listing of it. Both are decided the same way every time and the reasoning is on each row, so a reader can flip one and rerun.
rule.scope_note: Soundness is about identity only. Nothing here reads or weighs an audit finding: the question asked of every pair is whether the report is ABOUT this scheme, never what it concluded.
rule.sound: the registry entry names the programme the report audited, and the entry's jurisdiction is one the report covers. A union audit of a national scheme may match a state's listing of that same national scheme, because the register deliberately under-merges and one scheme can hold several rows.
rule.wrong: anything else: the entry is a budget head, a body, a ministry or an accounting line rather than a scheme; the entry is a component, a sibling, a successor or an award attached to the audited scheme rather than the scheme itself; the entry is a different state's scheme that happens to share a generic name; or the join is matcher noise with no relation between the two names.

matcher_defects.note: the legitimate case the rule exists for, DAY-NRLM against its expansion, has the same shape: one written acronym inside one derived initialism. What separates them is that nrlm is the TAIL of daynrlm and covers most of it, while smam is four letters of twelve. A position and coverage test would keep DAY-NRLM and reject all four pairs above, but it is not made here.
matcher_defects.what: the rule requires one side to be an acronym somebody wrote, `x in wa or y in wb`. It does not require the OTHER side to be one, so a written acronym matches any long initialism that happens to contain those four letters anywhere. Initialisms derived from audit titles are long, and audit titles are sentences, so the collisions are constant: this rule produced 153 of the 398 joins and 150 of those are wrong, P(sound) 0.020.

matcher_defects.defect: a plural defeats every rule, including the ones that decide absence

examples.a: Scheme for Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of (Hybrid &) Electric Vehicles
examples.b: Scheme for Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of (Hybrid and) Electric Vehicle in India - (FAME - India).

matcher_defects.note: FAME is one of the two absences this register has verified by hand, and the CAG audited it: report 125966. The audit and the scheme do not join, and the only difference between the shared halves of the two names is a trailing s. Folding a plural is the single cheapest change available to the matcher and 15 pairs on this corpus turn on it.
matcher_defects.what: `vehicles` and `vehicle` are different tokens and different skeletons, so content-word containment fails, the skeleton rule fails, and similarity carries the pair alone. This is a FALSE NEGATIVE and therefore the expensive direction: probably_same exists to decide absence, and a missed match is a claim that a portal omits something.
matcher_defects.where: tokens and skeleton, which do no singularisation

rule.clause: the matcher's reason is name evidence, not an acronym
rule.detail: similarity, content-word containment or transliteration; or the prefix rule where the REGISTRY name is the prefix of the subject rather than the other way round, and is not subordinated by a following under, through or within
rule.measured: the two acronym rules are P(sound) 0.019 over 258 pairs and the prefix rule as probably_same applies it is 0.052 over 58. Taking the name-evidence families alone lifts precision from 0.126 to 0.512 and costs 8 sound joins, of which the PAHAL and UDAN compliance audits are the two real losses.

rule.clause: the report is a Performance audit
rule.detail: a Performance audit is a study OF something and its title names that something. A Compliance or Financial audit is a sweep of a department and its title names the department.
rule.measured: P(sound) 0.211 over 228 against 0.012 over 164 for Compliance. Inside the name-evidence families every one of the 42 sound joins is a Performance audit and all 10 non-Performance joins are wrong.

rule.clause: the registry entry is not a union budget line the classifier calls a budget head
rule.detail: data/classification.json, keyed on the budget name the registry merged from. This is the schemes-versus-budget-heads test that made Karnataka's 621 and Andhra Pradesh's 552 unpublishable, arriving here as National Highways Authority of India, Estates Management, Projects of the Air Force, Electrification Projects and Recapitalization of Public Sector Banks.
rule.measured: P(sound) 0.029 over the 70 pairs whose entry is a classified budget head. It costs 2 sound joins, Border Area Development Programme and Modernisation of Police Forces, both of which the classifier itself gets wrong at score 0.

rule.clause: the two names agree in the right direction
rule.detail: every content word of the REGISTRY name appears in the subject; or the names are equal once normalised; or similarity is 0.78 or better; or the registry name's consonant skeletons are inside the subject's with at least three skeletons of three characters or more; or the subject's words are all inside the registry name and the only extra words are generic ones such as national or mission.
rule.measured: takes precision from 0.667 to 0.800 inside the earlier clauses. It is the clause that rejects a component wearing its parent's name: the EPFO internship scheme under an audit of the EPFO, one displaced-families line under an audit of the whole Prime Minister's Development Package, Samagra Shiksha's uniform intervention under an audit of Samagra Shiksha.

rule.clause: a state myScheme record must belong to the government the report covers
rule.detail: a record myScheme tags State or State/ UT is that state's listing. Where the report is a state report and the record is another state's, the two are different schemes that share a generic name.
rule.measured: P(sound) 0.068 over the 146 pairs where the states disagree. This is the most expensive clause in the rule: it removes 6 wrong joins, the three Chhattisgarh social security pension joins among them, and costs 7 sound ones, because myScheme lists two national schemes, ICDS and Deendayal Upadhyay Gram Jyoti Yojana, only under a single state's page. Both losses are named in recall_lost.

scope_note: A pointer, not a verdict. This says an audit exists on a scheme and where to find it. It says nothing about what the audit found, whether the scheme works, or whether the auditor was satisfied, and nothing in this pipeline reads an audit report body.

signals_rejected.measured: P(sound) 0.131 for subjects of 60 characters or fewer against 0.122 for longer ones, a lift of +0.009 over 398 pairs. Both ends of the range are bad and they cancel: the long tail is shouted titles and derived initialisms, the short tail is bare state names.
signals_rejected.signal: the length of the CAG subject
signals_rejected.why_not: no signal at the threshold anyone would pick. The short end alone is a signal and a negative one, which the two-content-word measurement records, and the rule picks it up through the containment and prefix clauses rather than through a length cut.

signals_rejected.signal: the report covers the Union rather than a state
signals_rejected.why_not: confounded. The union reports in this corpus include the ministry sweeps whose titles name a ministry rather than a scheme, so the signal is really the audit type wearing a different hat, and the audit type is measured directly.

signals_rejected.measured: P(sound) 0.096 over 271 against 0.189 over 127 for budget-sourced rows
signals_rejected.signal: the registry entry carries a myScheme source at all
signals_rejected.why_not: circular for the question this file exists to answer. The finding worth having is which audited schemes are ABSENT from myScheme, and scoring myScheme presence would push down exactly the rows the answer is made of. The same reasoning is set out in parse/classify_andhra.py's why_not_myscheme.

source: Comptroller and Auditor General of India, audit report index, joined to data/registry.json

validation.note: precision is counted over the 202 labelled joins rather than estimated from a sample. The joins it gets wrong are named in known_errors and the sound joins it drops are named in recall_lost. Any kept join with no hand label is listed above and is counted in neither.
